messages:
Alex: Ran a 10k QPS sweep against the 6xA100 pool last night — hit a repeating microburst pattern. p95 stayed OK but p99 jumps from ~80ms to ~420ms for ~6s when we get a KV miss + kernel swap at the same time. Posting quick logs below. :eyeglasses:
Maya: ugh. do you have the timeline aligned with GPU-util and kernel-flip markers?
Alex: yes, timeline shows kernel_switch at t, then 120ms later kvmiss expands to full attention rebuild, then queue piles. snippet:
```
[23:02:12] kernel_switch model=redwood-v2->quant-8bit ctx=512
[23:02:12.12] kvcache:miss key=conv-req-#241
[23:02:12.25] attention:rebuild seq=128 take=310ms
[23:02:17] p99=420ms p95=95ms gpu_util=92%
```
Sam: high GPU util + long rebuild = saturation window. how big were your microbatches?
Alex: default per-request microbatch cap=32 for this model (we were testing lower but reverted).
Li: couple of thoughts: 1) kernel selection hysteresis seems too short — we flip kernels on transient load; 2) KV miss causes full attention path which is slow on quant kernels. maybe prefer fallback kernel for misses?
Priya: agree. fallback kernel for kvmiss looks reasonable. Also we should tune target utilization lower during volatile windows — aim for 70-80% headroom rather than 90+.
Maya: quick experiment plan: canary 1) microbatch_cap=12 2) kernel_swap_hysteresis=500ms 3) enable soft-admit for requests when queue depth grows beyond 200. run 30m and measure p95/p99 and tokens/sec.
Sam: +1. also record kv_miss ratio and per-kernel latency. if fallback kernel gives better tail even at slightly higher token cost, prefer it.
Li: small profiling note: nvprof shows that attention rebuild stalls kernel pipeline and blocks other streams for ~200-350ms on these quant kernels. switching to fp16-fallback avoids rebuild but increases token compute by ~18% — acceptable if p99 improves.
Alex: we should also try prefix/KV prewarm for long conversations — hits mostly when cache cold. but the microbursts were independent of convo length sometimes.
Priya: for admission control: let's set soft-admit to reject/drop non-critical background requests (embeddings/rerank low-priority) during microburst windows instead of hard shedding. log counts of dropped requests.
infra-bot: ALERT generated: microburst-spike-detected on pool-6A100 at 2025-11-02T23:02:17Z, affected hosts=3, p99 spike to 420ms, gpu_util >90% for 9s. Ticket created: INF-4123.
Maya: owner for canary = @Maya. I'll submit a small runtime config PR and schedule the 30m canary at 09:30 UTC. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/merge_requests/512
Sam: tests to run: 1) controlled kvmiss injection 2) cold cache ramp 3) high qps steady-state. capture p50/p95/p99 and gpu_util histograms.
Li: add kernel-level traces for swap decisions and timestamps for kvcache lookup so we can correlate.
Alex: expected success criteria: p99 reduction > 2x during microburst windows and no more than 10% drop in steady-state throughput.
Priya: if canary passes, rollout plan: 10% -> 30% -> 100% over 2h with automated rollback on p99 regressions.
Maya: noting follow-ups: a) evaluate fp16-fallback perf/cost tradeoffs b) prewarm heuristics for long-tail keys c) refine admit thresholds. I'll post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
Alex: thanks everyone. tagging @eng-sre for visibility. :pray:
